correctness.rationale: Under 1<s<S, m≥2, t→0, m→∞, mt→0, and m s^(−m)/t→λ<∞, the Bessel-Jacobi–Anger representation from the given harmonic boundary map supplies P=2a+R and Q=2β+R at the inner circle. Since J_{±1}=±t/2+O(t³), only j=±1 contribute at order t²: R(θ)=S t m s^(−m)(s^(−1)e^(imθ)−s e^(−imθ))+o(t²), giving max Re R= S(s−s^(−1)) λt²+o(t²). Higher |j| are o(t²) by exponential radial damping and factorial small-t Bessel bounds, uniformly on θ. β(t)/a(t)=κ−SD t²/(4T²)+O(t⁴); differentiating |2β+R|/|2a+R| in real R gives 1/(2a(0)²). Combining yields κ+[SD/(4T²)](2D²λ−1)t²+o(t²). The first-mode outer value tends to κ/s²<κ, and O(mt)=o(1) sidebands preserve the gap; P stays nonzero so the holomorphic dilatation maximum is attained at the inner circle. Degree and Jacobian yield a diffeomorphism. Substitution m log s = log(1/t)+log log(1/t)+C+o(1) gives λ=e^(−C)/log s and C*=log(2D²/log s), excluding the undecided exact λ* boundary. This uses uniform analytic asymptotics, not finite Fourier sampling.
